title: A/B Contamination Guardrails and Sampling Protocol (scratch)
body:
Purpose:
This scratch doc captures a concrete, implementable set of guardrails to avoid cross-cohort contamination during A/B and canary experiments for LLM features. Focus is on traffic sampling rules, data/telemetry partitioning, instrumentation hygiene, and low-friction ops checks so we can run more frequent but safe experiments.

Audience:
Product managers, experiment owners, SRE/observability, backend engineers implementing routing, privacy & security reviewers, and solutions engineers who run customer-facing experiments.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Define contamination as any shared state, cached artifacts, or user-visible side-channel that leaks between cohorts and can bias metric estimates.
- Default isolation: user-id hashing + request-scoped cache keys + explicit model-variant tags.
- Always enable cohort metadata headers (x-rw-experiment, x-rw-cohort) on all downstream calls and logs.
- Sampling: prefer deterministic hashing on stable id; avoid device/session-only keys for long-running metrics.
- Quick rollback triggers: sustained delta on safety signals OR traffic spill >0.1% for >10m.

Definitions / failure modes (working list):
- Cache contamination: shared prefix caches (KV, LRU) returning outputs primed by another cohort.
- Model warmup cross-effect: batch/kernels warmed by variant A that later serve B and change latency/cost metrics.
- Logging/labeling loss: downstream systems drop cohort headers, causing attribution leakage.
- Behavioral drift via user feedback loops: cohort experiences change user behavior that subsequently affects other cohorts (e.g., search ranking).
- Telemetry aggregation bleed: rollups that aggregate at host-level hide cohort assignments (histogram buckets without cohort tag).

Sampling protocol (recommended defaults):
1) Deterministic cohort assignment
   - Use SHA256(user_id || experiment_id) mod 10000 -> range-based assignment.
   - For anonymous flows with multiple identifiers, prefer persistent account_id over ephemeral session_id.
   - If only session_id available, keep experiment horizon <= 24h and mark as ephemeral.

2) Hash key hygiene
   - Canonicalize user IDs (trim, lowercase) before hashing.
   - If multi-tenant: include tenant_id in hash input.

3) Allocation and bucketing
   - Support percentiles in thousandths (0.01% granularity) for precise slices.
   - Reserve a ‘holdout’ bucket of at least 0.1% for observability-only traffic (pingback).

4) Sampling propagation
   - Every outbound HTTP/gRPC call must include: x-rw-experiment, x-rw-cohort, x-rw-assignment-timestamp.
   - Kafka/async events must tag messages with the same fields or a single provenance header.

5) Sticky assignment
   - For experiments > 1 day, persist assignment to user profile store (ttl configurable, default 30 days).

Implementation checklist (engineering owner: assign in PR) :
- [ ] Implement hashing helper lib (languages: go/py/ts) + unit tests.
- [ ] Instrument middleware to inject cohort headers at edge.
- [ ] Audit all downstream services for header passthrough compliance.
- [ ] Add cohort tag to long-term metrics pipelines (prometheus labels, kafka topics).
- [ ] Prefix KV/cache keys with experiment_id:Cohort (e.g., exp123-A:prompt-prefix:{user}).
- [ ] Simulation run: synthetic traffic to validate no-spill guarantees (scripts + checklist).

Observability and signal surface (what to monitor):
- Traffic integrity signals:
  - % of requests with cohort header present (goal: 100%).
  - Host-level cohort distribution drift (compare expected vs observed per-host).
- Contamination detectors:
  - Cross-cohort cache hit correlation: when user assigned to cohort A sees responses that contain cohort-B-only tokens/markers.
  - Unexpected cohort churn per user (assignment flips > threshold over short time window).
- Safety & quality metrics:
  - Safety exception rate by cohort (toxic content flags, rejection rate).
  - Quality regressions (narrowed by guardrail thresholds defined per-metric).
- Cost/latency metrics:
  - Warmup-spill: abrupt latency decreases in cohort B following increased traffic to cohort A (indicates kernel reuse effect).

Quick decision matrix (operational):
- Incident types -> immediate action
  - Data contamination (evidence of cross-cohort content): abort experiment, snapshot logs, enable full sampling to reproduce, notify legal if PII/misuse suspected.
  - Telemetry loss (headers dropped): pause experiment traffic, roll back to baseline routing, kick off audit runbook.
  - Safety spike in variant: immediate rollback of variant to baseline for affected tenant(s), keep subset holdout for forensic logs.

Rollback thresholds (suggested, configurable per experiment):
- Safety signal: 3x baseline rate for 5 continuous minutes OR absolute increase of 0.05% if baseline low.
- Contamination indicator: detection of cross-cohort content in >= 10 distinct sessions within 15 minutes.
- Telemetry health: cohort-header presence < 99% for > 10 minutes.
- Cost impact: >20% increase in p95 token cost relative to baseline sustained > 30m.

Operational runbook snippets (for oncall):
- Check 1: Are cohort headers present in the ingress logs for recent requests (last 15m)? If not, redeploy edge middleware with header passthrough.
- Check 2: Query cache metric dashboards for experiment prefix misses/hits. If sudden cross-cohort hits observed, stop writes to that cache namespace and set TTL to 0 to flush.
- Check 3: Reconstruct session path for affected users: identify first variant exposure and subsequent cross-exposure.

Open design questions / things to validate in pilot:
- Should we enforce per-host cohort pinning to eliminate warmup cross-effect? Pros: stronger isolation. Cons: skewed host-level distribution and complexity for autoscaling.
- How to instrument third-party models (when using external hosted models) where we cannot control cache keys? Workaround: extra request-level attribution + stricter sampling horizons.
- Recommendation for synthetic warmup lanes: run micro-warmup traffic for each variant on isolated hosts before exposure. Need cost vs benefit study.
- Do we create a global ‘experiment registry’ to allocate safe cache namespaces and prefixes automatically? Prototype: small service that mints experiment ids and recommended prefixes.

Notes / stray ideas (brainstormy):
- Consider embedding a tiny cohort watermark token into model prompts for debug-only builds (strip in production) to help detect content bleed in sanitized logs.
- Create a ‘contamination-sim’ harness that replays production traffic to a sandboxed infra to estimate contamination risk for new rollout shapes.

Immediate next steps (owners marked):
- Priya: draft SDK spec for hashing helper and header format (due 2026-02-28).
- Ethan: inventory of services that read/write KV prefixes and current key-format (due 2026-02-18).
- Marisol: prototype detection queries for cross-cohort tokens (kafka + eventstore) and share example alert rules (due 2026-03-04).
- Jonah: cost study for host-per-cohort warmup approach (due 2026-03-10).

Back-of-envelope risk table (for launch checklist):
- Low risk: ephemeral UI tweaks with no cross-user state (use standard sampling).
- Medium risk: features with per-user cache or embeddings (require prefixed keys + short persistence).
- High risk: ranking/model-level changes that affect aggregated artifacts (require host isolation + longer holdouts + manual QA).

References and links:
- Confluence: Experiment Playbook (linked above)
- Internal: rollout-tooling PR that added experiment headers (github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-tooling/pull/412)
- Slack threads: #experiments (thread: 2025-11-12 "cache-prefixing for AB")

Appendix: example header spec (proto-style, plain text)
- x-rw-experiment: exp123
- x-rw-cohort: A
- x-rw-assignment-ts: 2026-02-21T19:02:03Z
- x-rw-assignment-src: hashing|profile-store

Concluding note: this is intentionally pragmatic — aim for minimal friction on experiment authors while raising the bar on contamination detection. We should pilot on 2-3 mid-weight experiments next quarter and iterate based on real incidents.

-- end of scratch doc --
